newsitem.title: TURKEY: Crowds gather for Turkish "Grey Wolf" funeral.
newsitem.headline: Crowds gather for Turkish "Grey Wolf" funeral.

text.p: Large crowds gathered in heavy snow in the Turkish capital on Tuesday for the funeral of far-right leader Alparslan Turkes who died at the weekend.

Thousands of mourners chanting nationalist slogans and carrying red-and-white Turkish flags blocked one of the city's main arteries as they waited for the funeral car to take the body of Turkes from a hospital to a ceremony in parliament.

Turkes, known as "Basbug" (Chieftain), died of a heart attack on Saturday aged 80. He was the veteran head of the Nationalist Action Party which campaigned to unite all Turkic peoples from the Balkans through Turkey to Central Asia.

His followers, known as "Grey Wolves", were involved in street fighting between rightists and leftists in the late 1970s in which more than 5,000 people were killed. The violence prompted the army to launch its third coup in as many decades.
His party remains a powerful influence in Turkish public life despite failing to win the 10 percent of the vote needed to field any MPs at 1995 general election.
President Suleyman Demirel, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and political party leaders were expected to attend a service for Turkes at Ankara's main Kocatepe mosque later in the day.
Police shut roads in central Ankara in anticipation of tens of thousands of mourners.

Buses carrying nationalists from all over the country as well as Turkish communities in Cyprus and the Balkans have been arriving in Ankara over the last few days for the funeral, to be broadcast live on several television channels.
